answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with proof-of-burn identity bonds: registering an identity requires permanently burning a small amount of currency, a cost trivial for one honest agent but multiplied linearly across a fake swarm. Like water in a desert, value that is burned cannot be reused — a dune of ten thousand fake identities needs ten thousand separate burns, while a lone oasis of honest agents pays once and keeps trading. Every burn leaves an echo on the public ledger, so the cost of forgery is visible and permanent.
